open_decisions.title: Restricted collision telemetry for a SHA-256 uniqueness collision is not emitted
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-078 (S-07-004 contract lens)
open_decisions.note: SEARCH_CRAWL_RETRIEVAL.md § Frontier And Deterministic Selection sets four obligations on a hash collision: retain both SHA-256 and full preimage, allocate a collision ordinal, NEVER merge candidates, and 'emit restricted collision telemetry and follow the Volume I integrity result' (also AC-SM-006). S-07-004 implements the first three; the fourth is NOT built — the tranche creates no telemetry surface and the frontier is a technical execution record with no ledger writer of its own. Practical risk is nil (a SHA-256 collision cannot occur), so this is a record-honesty item, not a defect: the migration comment was corrected from claiming exact conformance. The same obligation applies to every other deduplication_keys consumer, so it belongs with a platform telemetry surface rather than S-07.

open_decisions.title: The same-Organization CROSS-PROJECT defect class has now appeared in three consecutive tranches

open_decisions.title: Sitemap discovery has no scheduler re-entry after sustained host-gate contention
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-081 (ADR-026 concurrency lens); DELIVERED by S-07-012 and CLOSED BY EXPLICIT TRANSFER at its acceptance, recorded as ADR-096
open_decisions.closure: CLOSED 2026-07-30 BY TRANSFER, NOT BY COMPLETION, and the distinction is the whole point of this field. WHAT WAS DELIVERED AND IS NOW PROVEN: the scheduler re-entry this item asked for exists. `Workflows::Wf005::CrawlDriver` honours the `retry_after` instant the sitemap gate release reports and re-enters `Workflows::Wf005::Admission`'s `run_byte_budget_contended` outcome, both of which were unreachable while nothing in production drove crawl execution. Sustained host-gate contention no longer terminalizes `sitemap_unavailable` with zero network attempts. WHAT IS NOT DELIVERED AND IS TRANSFERRED WHOLE TO S-07-009: deriving :450's `sitemap_unavailable` for a `crawl_host_gates` row that no production path can now terminalize. `Workflows::Wf005::DiscoverSitemaps` writes that terminal outcome only once the run has expired, while `Workflows::Wf005::CrawlDriver` halts on the same wall clock BEFORE it calls discovery with the same `now` — so the gate stays `pending` forever and FU-9's own sentence 'a host that stays contended until the deadline is terminalized honestly HERE, once, with unavailable' is unreachable. S-07-009 is the correct and only successor: BUILD_PLAN gives it 'terminal checkpoint + coverage/completion + CancelCrawl', it owns `crawls.coverage_status`, `crawls.completion_reason` and `crawl_terminal_outcomes`, and it already carries the two structurally identical obligations FU-21 and FU-22 name. NO PART OF THIS ITEM BELONGS ANYWHERE ELSE: FU-28 changes the unit of execution rather than coverage derivation, and S-07-011 owns the stranded-claim sweep (FU-22), not this. This item is closed so it cannot be double-counted; the obligation is alive in S-07-009's BUILD_PLAN preconditions, which is where the next tranche will read it.
open_decisions.note: A host under sustained contention can exhaust MAX_DEFERRALS_PER_CANDIDATE and terminalize `sitemap_unavailable` with zero network attempts — write-once, coverage partial. Mitigated (the gate now reports the REAL remaining wait, so pacing no longer expires on a legitimate Crawl-delay) but not closed. S-07-008 owns run scheduling and MUST provide the re-entry; if it does not, this becomes a coverage defect and reopens S-07-006. MITIGATED, NOT DELIVERED, by S-07-008 (b1dcea9), and NOT closed. The ADR-026 architecture and concurrency lenses were right that a hand-back method is not scheduler re-entry: nothing in production calls `DiscoverSitemaps#call` at all, so 'the next pass claims it exactly as the first did' presupposes a pass that does not exist. What S-07-008 genuinely removed is the write-once FALSE outcome: sustained contention no longer terminalizes. :450 conditions `sitemap_unavailable` on 'no candidate succeeds AFTER retries/validation'; a candidate the rate limiter never released has had neither, so nothing is recorded - the claim is handed back (`release_sitemaps`, token-bound), the gate returns to `pending`, and the next pass claims it exactly as the first did. NO new scheduled-action kind: the catalogue is closed and a `pending` gate IS the re-entry. Bounded by the run's wall clock, past which discovery terminalizes `unavailable` once, honestly. NOT closed until the five ADR-026 lenses report (ADR-080). The DRIVER is now owned by BUILD_PLAN S-07-012 (Crawl Execution - the run driver), which must honour the `retry_after` instant the release reports and must also re-enter `Admission`'s `run_byte_budget_contended` outcome. FU-9 closes when S-07-012 lands, not before. A SECOND defect found by the same review and repaired here: the run-wide sitemap-document budget was charged BEFORE the gate was consulted and had no release path, so every deferred pass shrank the budget and the re-entry converged on the very `sitemap_unavailable` outcome FU-9 exists to prevent; the charge now happens once per distinct URL at the moment an attempt genuinely begins. S-07-008 IS ACCEPTED (ADR-083) with FU-9 MITIGATED, not closed: nothing in production drives crawl execution, so a hand-back method is not scheduler re-entry. The obligation is now S-07-012's, which is the next eligible block and depends on S-07-008. NOT CLOSED AT S-07-012, and the reason is recorded in ADR-090. The re-entry this item asked for IS delivered and no false outcome is written, but FU-9's own sentence 'A host that stays contended until the deadline is terminalized honestly HERE, once, with `unavailable`' is no longer reachable on any production path: `DiscoverSitemaps#defer_to_scheduler?` terminalizes only once the run has expired, and `CrawlDriver#advance` halts on the wall clock before it calls discovery, with the same `now`. The gate therefore stays `pending` forever and deriving :450's `sitemap_unavailable` from that state becomes S-07-009's obligation. FU-9 is DELIVERED-WITH-A-CARRIED-OBLIGATION rather than closed, so it must not be closed silently. THAT CONDITION IS NOW SATISFIED AND THE ITEM IS CLOSED: see the `closure` field above, which states what was delivered, what was not, and names S-07-009 as the receiving block; the obligation is also written into S-07-009's own BUILD_PLAN preconditions so the successor reads it there rather than having to find it here.

open_decisions.title: A terminal Crawl may carry NULL coverage_status and NULL completion_reason
open_decisions.authority: ADR-026 schema lens at S-07-008 (third pass, MISDIAGNOSED), corrected by the fourth pass; REPAIRED as S-07-009's blocking precondition, recorded as DECISIONS ADR-097
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED 2026-07-30 by `20260727120340_crawls_terminal_completeness`, as the first act of S-07-009 rather than inside it, because S-07-009 writes exactly the two columns this admits NULL. THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, and that is why the repair is recorded with its refutations. Pass three called it a three-valued-logic hole in `crawls_coverage_status_check` and prescribed the `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` form; THAT IS A PROVEN NO-OP, re-verified live at the repair: a CHECK admits the UNKNOWN the current form yields AND the TRUE the rewrite yields, so applying it would have produced a diff, closed the item and left the hole open. `crawls_coverage_status_check` is therefore DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED, and PROOF 29 pins the no-op so it cannot be reintroduced as a fix. THE ACTUAL DEFECT was ordinary two-valued logic in `crawls_terminal_shape`, whose terminal limb required only `terminal_at IS NOT NULL` — measured live, it admitted `state='completed'` with both `coverage_status` and `completion_reason` NULL, `completed` with a reason and no coverage, and `failed` with neither. THE REPAIR IS SCOPED BY STATE and the scoping IS the repair: every terminal state requires `completion_reason IS NOT NULL`, and `state='completed'` additionally requires `coverage_status IS NOT NULL`. The naive 'every terminal state needs BOTH' form is wrong and was DEMONSTRATED wrong as a mutation: it breaks `IdentityAccess::Infrastructure::CrawlStartStore#fail`, the only production writer of `completion_reason`, which records `failed` with a reason and no coverage because a Crawl that failed before execution retrieved nothing there is coverage to report on — and it also fails two PRE-EXISTING accepted examples. PROOFs 26-29, plus two mutations (the conjunct removed; the naive both-columns form), each failing named examples. The catalogue's nullable declaration is reconciled in `schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md`: the columns stay nullable and the state-scoped completeness rule is stated alongside them. The three genuine three-valued-logic holes found by the same sweep are separate and still open under FU-12: `identity_receipt_nonces.bootstrap_digest_only_for_bootstrap_purposes`, `invitations.invitation_active_expiry_is_seven_days`, `projects.projects_local_profile_shape`.

open_decisions.title: Non-blocking backlog carried out of S-07-008's third review pass
open_decisions.authority: ADR-026 lenses at S-07-008, third pass. Recorded rather than repaired, to avoid widening an unaccepted tranche.
open_decisions.note: (a) `crawl_limit_decisions.decided_by_service_identity_id` carries NO FK to `service_identities`, unlike every other Service-Identity reference in the schema, so `Platform::ServiceIdentity`'s 'existence is guaranteed by the ledger foreign keys' does not hold for it and the migration's 'a limit decision has an author' is unenforced. (b) `specification/automation/BUILD_PLAN.yml` DOES NOT PARSE AS YAML (Psych: could not find expected ':' at line 506) - PRE-EXISTING at both endpoints of the S-07-008 range, but it weakens the guarantee that the controller reads `depends_on`, which S-07-009's new comment rests on. (c) `DECISIONS.md` ADR-081 still reads 'that re-entry is S-07-008's' with no supersession note; the reassignment to S-07-012 must be carried into whatever ADR accepts S-07-008. (d) `crawl_sitemap_document_charges` lacks `UNIQUE (organization_id, project_id, id)`, which every sibling crawl table carries per POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA :128 - no live defect (nothing FKs to it) but a future child could not form the three-column link. (e) WITHDRAWN - the index `crawl_sitemap_document_charges_crawl` is NOT dead and must not be dropped. It was recorded as dead from a scan count taken BEFORE the same commit made it load-bearing: `charged_count` and the projection recompute both resolve through its `(organization_id, crawl_id)` prefix, and the ledger's ceiling enforcement now depends on it. Retained here as a correction rather than deleted, because a backlog item that directs the removal of a load-bearing index is exactly the false premise this review exists to catch. (f) `EffectiveLimits.resolve`'s rescue is method-wide, so ONE unparseable policy discards EVERY valid narrowing policy; behaviour is unchanged from the copies it replaced but this is now the canonical statement. (g) once the sitemap budget is spent, remaining candidates still claim and release a real host-gate slot and re-run FetchAuthorization before discovering they cannot pay.

open_decisions.title: VERIFICATION_MANIFEST names two mandatory check paths that have never existed
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-083 (found running the authoritative gate set at S-07-008 acceptance)
open_decisions.note: `specification/automation/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.yml` declares `controller_locking` -> `bundle exec rspec spec/automation/locking` and `controller_crash_recovery` -> `bundle exec rspec spec/automation/crash_recovery`, both `mandatory: true` under `fail_on_missing_required_check: true`. NEITHER DIRECTORY HAS EVER EXISTED: `git log --all -- spec/automation/locking spec/automation/crash_recovery` is empty. Every prior accepted tranche touched `specification/automation/**` and so matched the `controller_code` check set, which means these two checks have never run and their absence was never recorded. Related coverage exists under other paths (`spec/automation/integration/git_lock_record_spec.rb` for locking; `spec/automation/unit/state_machine_spec.rb` and `build_state_spec.rb` for resumption), so the repair is either to write the two suites at the declared paths or to reconcile the manifest onto the paths that hold the coverage. NOT caused by and NOT blocking S-07-008, which changed controller DATA and no controller code. A manifest that names a check nobody runs is the same class of defect as prose that names a mechanism nobody built.

open_decisions.title: Shared test-harness PG connections were unbounded and could hang the mandatory suite gate
open_decisions.authority: Found 2026-07-30 running the mandatory gate set; blocks any commit that requires a green complete_test_suite
open_decisions.note: CORRECTED AND REPAIRED. The original record got the ownership WRONG in two ways and both are withdrawn here. (1) It said the defect belonged to 'S-013'. THERE IS NO S-013 BLOCK IN BUILD_PLAN - the name was inferred from a commit-message prefix and a spec filename, which is exactly the inference that must not be made, and the repository-truth block-citation check does not match that token so it passed unvalidated. (2) It located the defect in the WF-013 concurrency specs. It is not there. THE ROOT CAUSE, PROVEN ON DEMAND RATHER THAN INFERRED: `config/database.yml` sets a statement timeout and states its purpose - 'A conservative statement timeout keeps a contended lock in a test from hanging the suite'. ActiveRecord applies it via `variables:`; a raw `PG.connect` does not and inherits the server default of 0, meaning UNLIMITED. Measured: the harness connection reported `0`, the ActiveRecord connection `15s`. `ReceiptMinter#truncate_all` then issues the suite's most lock-hostile statement - TRUNCATE over 26 tables with RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on all of them - from an `after` hook on essentially every acceptance example. With one session merely idle in a transaction that had SELECTed from `organizations`, that TRUNCATE on a harness-style connection was still blocked after 20 seconds; the identical statement carrying database.yml's value raised `PG::QueryCanceled`. The WF-013 specs were where the pile-up was VISIBLE because they spawn threads, not where the defect lived. REPAIRED in commit 0c1aa43 by routing the two MEMOIZED process-wide harness connections through `PgTestConnection`, which applies database.yml's own variables. No timeout was widened, no test serialised, no assertion removed, no concurrency reduced: a bound was introduced where there was none. `race_harness` and `scheduled_action_harness` are deliberately exempt - per-example, closed in an `ensure`, and the former exists to make connections block against each other. EVIDENCE: before, two of four whole-suite runs hung; after, four consecutive runs at 1894/0. Guarded by four mutation-verified assertions in `spec/architecture/test_harness_connection_bounds_spec.rb`. REOPENED 2026-07-30 on owner instruction, and correctly so: closing it confused a BOUND with a DISPROOF. What is repaired is the UNBOUNDEDNESS. If the underlying lock contention recurs it will now surface as a `PG::QueryCanceled` naming its statement rather than as a hang, which is what database.yml says the setting is for. FU-15 THEREFORE STAYS OPEN. Four consecutive clean whole-suite runs are evidence that the symptom is gone, not proof that the contention is: the lock contention that made an unbounded wait reachable has never been demonstrated absent, only prevented from stopping the run. It closes when the contention itself is disproved - or when it recurs as a `PG::QueryCanceled` naming its statement, which would identify the holder and make the real fix possible. Fixing a gate does not establish the underlying behaviour. NEW EVIDENCE, 2026-07-30, from running five independent reviewers concurrently against one `f1_test`: three of them independently hit the contention and NAMED THE HOLDER. Observed as `PG::TRDeadlockDetected` on `crawl_policies` and as backends wedged on `INSERT INTO crawl_host_gates` and `TRUNCATE identity_receipt_nonces`, in every case blocked behind `ReceiptMinter#truncate_all`'s `TRUNCATE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE` taking ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. Whole-suite runs under that contention reported 6, 279, 292, 294, 295 and 297 failures and one hang; with nothing else touching the database the suite is 1921/0, reproduced on three consecutive runs. This is the recurrence FU-15's closure condition asked for - it names the statement and identifies the holder - and it CONFIRMS the reopening was right: the bound converted a hang into cascading cancellations, it did not remove the contention. FU-15 STAYS OPEN. The trigger was the implementation agent's own decision to run five reviewers in parallel against one test database, which is the operational lesson: the suite is not safe to run concurrently with itself.

open_decisions.title: OWNER DECISION: does the first crawl_fetch_due PRE-ADMIT at start, or admit at execution?
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-085 (owner ruling HD-S07-FU16-FIRST-HANDOFF, 2026-07-30)
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED by owner ruling, recorded as ADR-085: option (B). StartCrawl schedules the first `crawl_fetch_due` against the SELECTED FRONTIER ENTRY; fetch admission remains the SOLE producer of `fetch_attempts`; admission occurs ONLY at execution; S-07-007's proven retry semantics are unchanged; no second producer is introduced. The withdrawn (3/n) pre-admit patch is discarded rather than committed. Consequences carried into S-07-012: `crawl_fetch_due` carries `target_type = 'crawl_frontier_entry'`, and (2/n)'s attempt-prepare limb is REMOVED rather than kept beside the new one - `FetchAttemptDueSchedule`, `FetchAttemptStore#prepare`/`#claim_prepared`/`#submission_started` and `FetchContent#record_persisted_attempt` existed only to make a pre-created attempt executable, so retaining them would BE the second producer the ruling forbids. Corroborated by the ratified catalogue itself: :140-143 give the ingestion/parsing/indexing/check kinds as "initial or declared 30/120-second retry", while :138 gives `crawl_fetch_due` no retry limb at all, because :444's content-fetch retries are the in-process loop S-07-007 proved. The residual :138/:185 naming divergence (their prose names a Fetch Attempt as the claim owner) is carried as FU-17 for prose reconciliation, not resolved by inventing a row to point at.

open_decisions.title: BACKGROUND_PROCESSING :138/:185/:198 name a Fetch Attempt as `crawl_fetch_due`'s claim owner; ADR-085 makes it the frontier entry
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-085 (owner ruling HD-S07-FU16-FIRST-HANDOFF); raised at S-07-012
open_decisions.note: PROSE RECONCILIATION, not a behavioural defect. :185 says "the action's `target_id` is the direct claim-owner row ID" and :198 records `crawl_fetch_due`'s direct claim owner as "Fetch Attempt"; :138 describes it as "one selected persisted fetch attempt, including an immediate first attempt". ADR-085 rules that the action targets the SELECTED FRONTIER ENTRY, because under admission-at-execution no attempt row exists at scheduling time and creating one would make the scheduler a second producer. Nothing is unsound: the frontier entry IS a claim owner (`queued -> in_progress` under the frontier's own advisory lock is the claim), and the durable idempotency authority is unchanged - the attempt identity `(crawl_host_gate_id, request_kind, crawl_frontier_entry_id, attempt_number)` under its ON CONFLICT, derived from the entry and the attempt number. What is unreconciled is the CATALOGUE PROSE, which still names the row that no longer exists at scheduling time. The repair is a wording change in `specification/volume-ii/BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md` naming the claim owner as "the selected frontier entry, whose fetch attempts carry the durable idempotency identity" - a ratified-document edit, so it is recorded here rather than taken inside an implementation tranche. WIDENED at S-07-012's review (contract lens): the divergence is not confined to the catalogue's dispatch-registry prose. `crawl_frontier_entry` now also appears as `command_executions.target_type`, in `command_results.target_refs`, as `idempotency_records.target_type` and as the audit record's `entity_type`. `specification/volume-ii/API_CONTRACTS.md` declares the entity-type vocabulary CLOSED in major 1 and contains `fetch_attempt` but not `crawl_frontier_entry`, and every other TARGET_TYPE in the repository is a member of it - this is the first that is not. MTX-030 `persistence_model` also says the frontier queue MUST NOT be promoted to a product entity. Nothing is unmet today because no domain event is emitted on this path and the audit table constrains neither column, but the reconciliation is wider than first recorded.

open_decisions.title: ARCHITECTURAL STOP CONDITION: the frontier seal release (in_progress -> terminal) is refused by an accepted proof
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-087 (owner ruling on FU-18, 2026-07-30)
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED by owner ruling, recorded as ADR-087: DELIVER the `in_progress -> terminal` seal release in S-07-012, which owns the dequeue-and-fetch decision and therefore owns the compare-and-set terminal transition that releases `sealed_depth`. Boundaries held and each one asserted: `terminal` reachable from `in_progress` only; the transition is a compare-and-set on `(state = 'in_progress', state_version)`; `fetched_pending_commit` stays EXCLUDED (:456's coordinator limb, which arrives with concurrent fetching and link extraction); no edge leaves `terminal`; `commit_order` remains S-07-009's; `crawl_terminal_outcomes` and the link-extraction/coordinator path remain S-07-009's and S-07-010's. The obsolete assertion in `spec/persistence/crawl_frontier_invariants_spec.rb` is REPLACED by a stronger one rather than deleted, and the stale ownership comment in `spec/acceptance/wf005_crawl_frontier_spec.rb` is corrected in the same commit as the migration. The transition is taken in the DRIVER's own transaction, immediately after the fetch and before the ledger and the next link: retiring it inside the handler's terminal transaction would leave a process lost mid-pass with an entry `in_progress` forever and the depth PERMANENTLY PINNED, needing a resumption policy S-07-012 has no authority to invent, whereas retiring it first leaves the seal released so the redelivery records `superseded` and links the run on.

open_decisions.title: BLOCKING FOR S-07-012 ACCEPTANCE: a fetch pass can outlive its 30-second transport lease by 6x, so the ordinary retry path executes twice
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-089 (owner ruling on FU-19, 2026-07-30)
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED by owner ruling, recorded as ADR-089: SCHEDULER RE-ENTRY. A `crawl_fetch_due` execution performs at most ONE content-fetch attempt; a retryable outcome with attempts remaining schedules a new `crawl_fetch_due` for the SAME frontier entry at `fetch_attempts.completed_at` plus :444's delay, and the worker returns without waiting. The global worker lease is NOT extended. :444's three-attempt bound and its exact 30,000 / 120,000 ms delays are unchanged, attempt numbering still derives from committed state, and the frontier claim, the byte reservation and the depth seal are held across the retry because they belong to one admission of one URL. The retry instant is DERIVED from the committed row rather than taken from the worker's clock, which makes two deliveries compute the same ScheduledAction identity so the second replays instead of forking the chain. A retry that would fall past `crawls.deadline_at` is not created; it is treated as exhaustion, which releases the reservation and the seal immediately. ADR-089 SUPERSEDES ADR-085's in-process-retry clause and nothing else. Seven properties proved over the production-real chain and eight mutations each failing an example; the accepted S-07-007 pacing proof was translated from in-process sleeps to the reported delay sequence [30000, 120000, nil], asserted whole rather than as a prefix.

open_decisions.title: The pacing pre-check covers :442's rate floor only, not the concurrency ceiling, and robots is unpaced
open_decisions.authority: ADR-026 architecture and security lenses at S-07-012
open_decisions.note: `Workflows::Wf005::CrawlDriver#host_ready_at` reads `pacing_remaining_ms`, which is the `next_allowed_start_at` floor. It does NOT see `window_starts` or `active_connection_count`, so 'one pass makes at most one paced host start' is exact for the rate floor and silent on :442's concurrency ceiling; the check is also advisory and unlocked, while `HostGate#claim` remains the only enforcement. Separately, `Workflows::Wf005::EnsureRobots` takes no host-gate slot at all (it has no `claim_slot` call), so the driver's robots request is counted against neither the rolling-second rate nor the concurrency ceiling - a pass can make one UNPACED start in addition to its paced one. Both are pre-existing shapes of the accepted S-07-005 surface and neither is reachable as a defect on today's strictly sequential chain; both become reachable with :456's concurrent fetching, which is S-07-010's. NO LONGER LATENT in one respect: the rate-floor-only pre-check is the PRECONDITION of the concurrency lens's demonstrated defect, because two deliveries both pass `host_ready_at` and then one loses the gate claim. (8/n) removed the harm - a pass that performs no attempt now disposes of nothing - but the pre-check still sees neither `window_starts` nor `active_connection_count`, and `HostGate#claim` remains the only enforcement point.

open_decisions.title: BLOCKING FOR S-07-009: a terminal frontier entry can carry no fetch_attempts row, so a covered URL is indistinguishable from an unretrieved one
open_decisions.authority: ADR-026 schema lens at S-07-012, which demonstrated the guard's irreversibility live; ADR-088 corrects the ADR-087 premise it falsifies; RESOLVED at S-07-009 (3/n), recorded as DECISIONS ADR-098
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED 2026-07-31 by `Workflows::Wf005::CrawlDriver`, which now records exactly one `crawl_terminal_outcomes` row per entry it retires, IN THE SAME TRANSACTION AS THE SEAL RELEASE. THE DEFECT: `Workflows::Wf005::FetchContent` authorizes BEFORE it claims an attempt row, and :448's fail-closed robots host never reaches the fetch path at all, so an entry could be retired with NO attempt and a NULL `reason` — byte-identical to a fetched covered entry, and irreversible, because the frontier guard admits no edge out of `terminal`. THE TABLE WAS NOT THE FIX and S-07-009 (2/n) said so on its own terms ("FU-21 closes when the driver writes, not when the table exists"); this is the driver writing. BOTH retirement paths write — the decided fetch and the fail-closed host — and neither of the paths that retire nothing does: a `deferred` pass and a `superseded` redelivery record NOTHING, because the compare-and-set on the claim gates the write and `entry_once` is the backstop rather than the mechanism. ATOMICITY IS DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSERTED: PROOF 45 puts a conflicting row in the way so the INSERT must fail and requires the entry to be left `in_progress`; under the tidier two-transaction form it ends `terminal` with no classification, which is this defect with an extra step. TWO FIELDS ARE DERIVED IN SQL: `commit_order` is `MAX + 1` under the same per-Crawl frontier advisory lock that already orders admission, so :456's commit sequence IS the dequeue sequence by construction; `accounted_response_body_bytes` is SUMMED from the entry's committed content attempts per :301's "accounted byte totals", and the discriminator is exact because `FetchContent` classifies an HTTP error without a measurement — a 503's `Result#accounted_bytes` is 0 while its attempt row carries the real figure. `Workflows::Wf005::CoverageClassification` holds :452's outcome-to-effect map; it is the one duplication the design could not avoid (the CHECK's vocabulary lives in a migration class, unloadable at runtime) and PROOF 41 rebuilds the map from the LIVE `pg_constraint` definition and asserts it in both directions. PROOFs 41-42 (catalogue) and 43-49 (driver, production-real chain); three mutations, each failing named examples, one of them failing two PRE-EXISTING accepted examples. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: nothing READS these rows yet — the terminal checkpoint that derives `crawls.coverage_status` and `crawls.completion_reason` from them is the next slice of S-07-009 — and `document_id` stays NULL because Documents are S-07-010's, so `document_created` records CANDIDATE coverage exactly as the accepted migration recorded it. FU-22's stranded `in_progress` claim is untouched and remains S-07-011's.

open_decisions.title: A pass lost during the fetch strands its frontier claim in_progress, pinning sealed_depth for the life of the run
open_decisions.authority: ADR-026 concurrency and architecture lenses at S-07-012; ADR-088 corrects ADR-087's self-healing overstatement
open_decisions.note: The window between `Admission`'s claim and the seal release CONTAINS the network fetch, which is where losses actually happen. A loss there leaves the entry `in_progress`, and nothing recovers it: ADR-082 added a lease sweeper for `fetch_attempts`, not for frontier claims, and the guard admits no edge back to `queued`. On a single-Source run `peek_next` is then confined to the pinned `sealed_depth` and returns nil, so the run stops. WHAT S-07-012 FIXED IS THE FALSE REPORT: the pass now distinguishes a drained frontier from a PINNED one and says which, instead of claiming the crawl finished. WHAT REMAINS is the recovery, which needs the `in_progress` analogue of ADR-082's attempt-lease sweeper - a frontier-claim sweep with a lease - and that is recovery vocabulary, which BUILD_PLAN assigns to S-07-011 (recovery + replay). Bounded in the meantime by the run's 60-minute wall clock, WHICH IS NOW ACTUALLY ENFORCED: the second half of this item — 'nothing yet SCHEDULES `crawl_terminal_deadline`, so the bound is not currently enforced by anything either' — was DELIVERED at S-07-009 (6/n) under ADR-101. The accepted start now schedules the checkpoint at `crawls.deadline_at` on its own transaction, so a pinned run terminalizes at its deadline instead of staying `running` for ever. What REMAINS of this item is only the recovery: a frontier-claim sweep with a lease, the `in_progress` analogue of ADR-082's attempt-lease sweeper, which BUILD_PLAN assigns to S-07-011. The checkpoint deliberately does NOT schedule its early drained-run instant for a PINNED frontier, precisely so that recovery is not foreclosed by this tranche.

open_decisions.title: Two latent-concurrency guards in S-07-012 survive mutation and cannot be tested until concurrent fetching lands
open_decisions.authority: Recorded at S-07-012 rather than given fabricated tests
open_decisions.note: (a) `Workflows::Wf005::CrawlFetchDueSchedule#link_next` peeks under the frontier advisory lock; removing the lock changes no test, because only :456's concurrent fetching can produce the interleaving where two terminal transactions select the same candidate and fork the run into two chains. (b) `IdentityAccess::Infrastructure::CrawlFrontierStore#claim_next` is not restricted to the id `peek_next` returned - `Admission#claim_entry` tests the PEEK and then claims 'whatever is next' in a separate statement. Sound today because every writer of a `queued` row takes the same advisory lock; the one-line hardening is `AND e.id = $n` in `claim_next`'s CTE, threaded from the caller. Both are recorded as untested-by-construction rather than covered, because a test that cannot fail is worse than a recorded gap.

open_decisions.title: BLOCKING FOR S-07-012 ACCEPTANCE: a delivery can still outlive the 30-second worker lease, by two routes FU-19 did not close
open_decisions.authority: DECISIONS ADR-091 (owner ruling on FU-24, 2026-07-30), CORRECTED BY ADR-092 after two independent focused reviews each returned BLOCK
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED by owner ruling, recorded as ADR-091: a FENCED lease heartbeat, not a permanently longer lease. `WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` stays short so a dead worker is recovered promptly; a live worker renews while it still owns legitimate work. `f1_heartbeat_scheduled_action` matches the action identity, the claim owner, the claim generation, the `dispatched` state and a lease that has NOT already lapsed. Cadence is :288's ratified rule exactly — one third of the lease, floored to whole seconds, bounded 5 through 30 — driven by ELAPSED TIME, so heartbeat writes are bounded by duration rather than by redirect, sitemap or fetch counts. THREE CLAIMS IN THE ORIGINAL NOTE WERE FALSE AND ARE CORRECTED IN ADR-092, each having been DEMONSTRATED by review. (1) A relinquished delivery was SETTLED `completed`, not released: `f1_settle_scheduled_action` carries no lease predicate, so in the lapsed-but-unswept window the settle matches and the action completes having done nothing. (2) 'Redirect hops renew through the guard F-01 already calls' was true of the CONTENT path only; robots and sitemap fetches passed no `redirect_guard` while still following the ten-redirect budget, so each was up to eleven bounded requests and ~165 seconds behind ONE renewal, measured at zero heartbeat writes with the sweep then reclaiming the action. (3) 'No request, attempt, byte, terminal state, link or ledger row' was an intent, not a property: after a confirmed transfer the sitemap traversal kept requesting, spent run-wide budget, offered content URLs to the frontier and wrote the WRITE-ONCE gate outcome, and the robots path would have written a permanent fail-closed decision. ALL THREE ARE NOW REPAIRED and covered by PROOFs 12-16, each of which fails under a mutation of the line it covers. The previously-recorded surviving sitemap-boundary mutation was NOT untestable — PROOF 15 tests it with two candidates — and calling it a limitation was wrong. ONE MUTATION STILL SURVIVES and is recorded as defence in depth rather than a proven control: the `status = 'dispatched'` predicate is redundant with the owner/generation fence in every reachable state, because a non-`dispatched` row never carries the worker's owner. TWO RATIFIED :288/:290 CLAUSES REMAIN UNIMPLEMENTED and are escalated as FU-25 and FU-26.

open_decisions.title: BLOCKING FOR S-07-012 ACCEPTANCE: BACKGROUND_PROCESSING :288's LEASE DURATION rule is unimplemented, and the flat 30-second lease cannot survive ONE ratified redirect hop
open_decisions.authority: owner ruling 2026-07-30 (implement :288 lease derivation), recorded as DECISIONS ADR-094; REOPENED by the focused review of 0de3f3e and closed by the owner's second ruling, recorded as ADR-095
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED, BUT NOT ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT, AND THE FIRST RECORD OF THIS ITEM WAS FALSE. Recording that plainly, because the false record is the reusable lesson. WHAT WAS RULED: implement :288's ratified lease-duration rule rather than tune the flat lease. The producer stamps `scheduled_actions.product_attempt_deadline`, immutable under `f1_scheduled_actions_guard`, and the transport functions derive `lease_expires_at` from it and `transaction_timestamp()`. WHAT WAS FIRST BUILT AND WRONGLY RECORDED AS CLOSED (ADR-094): the derivation reached TWO of the THREE functions that assign a lease. `f1_heartbeat_scheduled_action` was untouched and still wrote the caller's flat value, which `Worker#lease_keeper_for` supplies as `WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` = 30 — so a `crawl_fetch_due` dispatched with a 900-second derived lease had it REWRITTEN TO 30 at the first renewal boundary, which `Lease.owned?` reaches within ten seconds of handler start, restoring byte-for-byte the state this item was raised to repair. This note previously said 'THE DEMONSTRATED DEFECT IS CLOSED... the interval clamps to 30 seconds, so the worst unguarded gap is 60 seconds against a 900-second lease'. BOTH HALVES WERE FALSE: the interval was 10, because the keeper divides the worker constant and not the derived lease, and the standing lease was 30, not 900. TWO FURTHER DEFECTS FOUND WITH IT: the cap was written `greatest(15 minutes, caller_request)`, which is not a cap above 900 at all (a caller passing 3600 received 3600, measured), and :288's own 30-second floor could not satisfy the invariant `lease > interval + max_hop` that the rule exists to guarantee, since `30 > 10 + 30` is false and the floor is reachable near a run deadline and for every kind that stamps no deadline. NOW GENUINELY CLOSED BY ADR-095: one canonical expression `least(greatest(caller_request, 60s, deadline - v_now + 30s), 15 minutes)` written into ALL THREE writers from a single migration string, the cap absolute, the ratified floor corrected to 60 in BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md :288 itself. Proved on the live functions by PROOFs 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, 25 and five mutations, each failing a named example; PROOF 25 and `spec/architecture/scheduled_action_lease_rule_spec.rb` are structural and would have caught the original defect, which no behavioural example did. THE RESIDUE IS FU-29, named rather than absorbed. ONE DESIGN NOTE WORTH KEEPING: the derivation was first extracted into a helper function and `spec/platform/scheduled_actions/store_spec.rb` correctly failed it, because any `%scheduled_action%` function taking a `timestamptz` violates :114. The arithmetic is therefore INLINED in all three functions. That gate caught a real shape defect and was not worked around.

open_decisions.title: BACKGROUND_PROCESSING :290's heartbeat AUTHORIZATION/POLICY CHECKPOINT is not verified: four of the five required predicates are implemented
open_decisions.authority: owner decision required (standing stop condition: authorization or RLS semantics); recorded by DECISIONS ADR-092
open_decisions.note: :290 requires a heartbeat transaction to verify owner, claim generation, nonterminal state, CURRENT AUTHORIZATION/POLICY CHECKPOINT, and unexpired lease before extending from database time. `f1_heartbeat_scheduled_action` implements four: `claim_owner`, `claim_generation`, `status = 'dispatched'` (stronger than 'nonterminal') and `lease_expires_at > v_now`. It never consults the executing Service Identity or any policy version, so a delivery whose authorization was revoked mid-execution keeps renewing until its work finishes. NOT TAKEN AS A REPAIR: what a 'current authorization/policy checkpoint' resolves to on a transport row served by one scheduler across every tenant is an authorization-semantics decision, and inventing one inside a SECURITY DEFINER function is precisely the class of change the standing stop conditions reserve. Note the related judgement recorded in ADR-092: the heartbeat increments `scheduled_actions.state_version`, which is read as the TRANSPORT row version and therefore within :290's 'never increments a product state version', but that is a reading rather than a fact.

open_decisions.title: PRE-EXISTING: the :444 robots retry path's `defer_robots` is not fenced against a stale-attempt takeover
open_decisions.authority: found by the third FU-24 focused review while confirming the relinquish-path repair; recorded by DECISIONS ADR-093
open_decisions.note: `EnsureRobots#decide`'s retry limb calls `defer_robots(gate_id, gate['state_version'], now)`, whose compare-and-set is against a `state_version` re-read under the row lock IN THE SAME TRANSACTION — so it can never fail against another owner, and its only real predicate is `robots_state = 'in_progress'`, which does not distinguish this worker's claim from a successor's. A worker whose fetch outlives `ATTEMPT_STALE_SECONDS` (300) can therefore revert a legitimate takeover, discarding the new owner's outcome and burning :444 attempts on a healthy host. THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT the third review demonstrated on the RELINQUISH path, which is repaired by fencing on `robots_generation` (`relinquish_robots`). The retry limb is pre-existing S-07-005 code and was NOT in FU-24's scope, so it is recorded rather than swept in — the owner's instruction was to repair only the confirmed heartbeat defect. The repair is the same shape: thread the claim's generation into `decide` and fence `defer_robots` on it.

open_decisions.title: NEXT TRANCHE: divide `crawl_fetch_due` into checkpointed members, then REMOVE the heartbeat
open_decisions.authority: owner ruling 2026-07-30 — sequenced as its own tranche so S-07-012 is accepted for what it implements; recorded as DECISIONS ADR-094
open_decisions.note: AMENDED BY ADR-095: the arithmetic below is unchanged, but note the lease it is measured against now has a 60-second floor and an ABSOLUTE 15-minute cap, and the heartbeat derives like the other two writers. Nothing in this item's case is weakened by that; the division is still owed. :288 ends 'A handler whose work can legitimately exceed 15 minutes divides it into checkpointed members; no individual claim exceeds the cap.' ONE `crawl_fetch_due` PASS CAN EXCEED IT BY FAR: the pass runs robots, then a sitemap traversal bounded at 50 documents each with up to 3 :444 attempts of ~30 seconds of hop time, then one content attempt. Ignoring :444's 30/120-second paces and the 20 gate deferrals per candidate entirely, that is already 50 x 3 x 30s = 75 minutes against a 15-minute cap. THE OWNER'S DIRECTION: the heartbeat is TRANSITIONAL INFRASTRUCTURE, not a destination. Divided so one execution performs at most one bounded outbound unit, the worst case per claim is one document (~5.5 minutes), the derived lease covers it BY CONSTRUCTION, and `LeaseKeeper`, `Lease`, `f1_heartbeat_scheduled_action` and every renewal boundary are deleted rather than maintained. That is ownership by construction instead of stateful ownership maintenance. WHY IT IS NOT PART OF S-07-012: it changes the UNIT OF EXECUTION, not a defect. It invalidates accepted S-07-005/006 proofs that assert a full traversal in one call, so it is a redesign crossing an accepted behavioural contract and deserves its own acceptance history and its own architectural review rather than being smuggled into a repair tranche. The re-entry mechanism already exists and needs no new vocabulary in the closed catalogue: `deferred` mints the next `crawl_fetch_due`, exactly as ADR-089 divided the :444 retries. CARRIES: FU-24's surviving `status = 'dispatched'` mutation and FU-27 both disappear with the heartbeat and the robots retry limb they belong to; re-check rather than assume. FU-29 also disappears with the heartbeat, so if FU-28 lands first it closes FU-29 rather than requiring it.

open_decisions.title: The heartbeat cadence is computed from the lease the worker REQUESTED, not the lease the database GRANTED
open_decisions.authority: owner ruling 2026-07-30 — deferred explicitly in the same ruling that repaired the lease derivation; recorded as DECISIONS ADR-095
open_decisions.note: :288 ties the heartbeat interval to THE LEASE DURATION: 'one third of the lease duration, rounded down to whole seconds and bounded from 5 through 30 seconds'. `Platform::ScheduledActions::LeaseKeeper#interval` divides `lease_seconds`, which `Worker#lease_keeper_for` supplies as the constant `WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` (30), NOT the value the transport function actually wrote to `lease_expires_at`. The worker has no way to learn it: `f1_dispatch_scheduled_action`'s `RETURNS TABLE` carries no `lease_expires_at` and `Store#to_action` maps no lease field. CONSEQUENCE, QUANTIFIED AND SAFE IN A NAMED DIRECTION: the interval is 10 seconds against a lease of at least 60 (ADR-095's floor) and up to 900, so the worker renews 2x to 3x more often than :288 requires, and never later. (THE RATIO IS 2x-3x, NOT 'three to ninety times', which an earlier draft of this note claimed: :288's own interval is itself clamped to a 30-second ceiling, so the cadence it requires is 20 seconds at the floor and 30 at the cap, against this worker's 10. Corrected here rather than quietly, because a false quantity in a deferral record understates or overstates a cost the owner is being asked to accept — in this case it overstated it.) The cost is heartbeat write amplification on `scheduled_actions` — each renewal also increments `state_version` and fires the row guard — plus a literal non-conformance with :288's cadence sentence. It is NOT a correctness gap, which is why it was deferred rather than rushed. WHY IT IS NOT REPAIRED IN ADR-095: the repair changes the RETURN SHAPE of a frozen F-04 transport function, which means `lib/f1/runtime_grants.rb`'s `PLATFORM_WORKER_FUNCTIONS` signature, `Platform::ScheduledActions::Store#to_action`, and `Action` must move together — a materially larger change than the defect repair it would have ridden in on, and one that touches the transport signature surface the owner's ruling explicitly declined to expand. TRIGGER: repair this when the dispatch function's return shape is next opened for any reason, or when heartbeat write volume becomes measurable, WHICHEVER IS FIRST. Note FU-28 deletes `LeaseKeeper` entirely, so if the checkpointed-member division lands first this item closes with it rather than being built.

open_decisions.title: `crawls.started_at` / `deadline_at` are writable after the accepted start, so the 60-minute ceiling is renegotiable by an UPDATE
open_decisions.authority: Found and deferred at S-07-009 (4/n) under ADR-099; RESOLVED at S-07-009 (9/n) on owner instruction, recorded as DECISIONS ADR-104
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED 2026-07-31 by `20260727120370_crawls_run_clock_immutable`, which widens the guard's run-identity limb to `started_at` and `deadline_at`. THE RULE: :442 fixes the wall clock at the `Queued -> Running` transition and BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md :139 fires `crawl_terminal_deadline` at exactly `deadline_at`, so a movable column made the sixty-minute ceiling ADVISORY — changeable by an UPDATE that alters no state and therefore meets no other check on the table. A column-level REVOKE could not express it, because the accepted start writes both columns through the same UPDATE privilege; the rule is 'not after `started_at` is set', a predicate over the row that only the trigger can carry. THE HARNESS COST WAS PAID RATHER THAN AVOIDED: all eight mutation sites across four spec files are gone, replaced by advancing the injected clock plus `Wf005CrawlChain#age_run_to`, which keeps :551's lease alive through the SAME `Entitlement::Service#heartbeat` every pass uses since FU-31 and at :551's own five-minute cadence. THIS IS WHY THE ITEM WAS BLOCKED ON FU-31 AND WHY THAT WAS RIGHT: before the heartbeat had a caller, a run could not honestly be sixty-one minutes old at all, so the replacement did not exist. ONE ACCEPTED EXAMPLE CHANGED WHAT IT ASSERTS, and the change is the fiction being removed: 'emits the wall-clock HARD limit' used `.sole`, which was only possible because its fixture produced a run past its deadline at ZERO elapsed minutes; with :442's ratified 45/60 pair a genuinely expired run always carries both crossings, so it now names the row it is about and adds `observed_value == 61`, which the old fixture could not have shown. PROOF 52 (extended, including `deadline_at = NULL`) and PROOF 90 (the catalogue facts plus a real UPDATE as the runtime role); one mutation, failing both.

open_decisions.title: BLOCKING FOR S-07-009's CHECKPOINT: nothing heartbeats a running Crawl's entitlement reservation, so every run is capped at 15 minutes and every commit degrades to a release
open_decisions.authority: WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md :551; MTX-030 transaction_boundary; found AND RESOLVED at S-07-009 (5/n), recorded as DECISIONS ADR-100
open_decisions.note: RESOLVED 2026-07-31 by `Workflows::Wf005::CrawlDriver#renew_entitlement_lease`, which renews :551's lease ON CADENCE from committed state, immediately after `authorize_run` establishes the run is live. THE DEFECT: `Platform::Entitlement::Service#heartbeat` was built by F-05 and HAD NO CALLER ANYWHERE. :551 requires 'a renewable lease with a heartbeat at least every 5 minutes'; `start_execution` sets `lease_due = now + 15 minutes` and nothing renewed it, so from the fifteenth minute every pass halted with `admission_entitlement_not_executing` (both `Admission#authorize_run` and `FetchAuthorization` test `lease_due > now`), :442's 60-minute wall clock was unreachable, and the terminal checkpoint's 'commit or release EXACTLY ONCE' would always have taken the RELEASE limb because `Service#commit` releases at or after the effective deadline — a completed Crawl with valid Documents never counted against the customer's entitlement. WHY IT WENT MISSING: BUILD_PLAN assigns S-22/WF-015 the `EntitlementLeaseRenewed` EVENT and says 'S-07 consumers invoke F-05 and record their OWN WF-005 outcomes; they never emit these' — the event was assigned and the INVOCATION was not. CADENCE, NOT PER PASS: `last_heartbeat_at` is on the reservation row, so two deliveries agree and a process loss cannot reset it; per-pass renewal would write one immutable row per fetch, the amplification F-04's LeaseKeeper already refused. PROOFs 54-57, of which PROOF 54 IS THE DEFECT asserted as a regression (a pass at minute sixteen halts on the entitlement with 44 minutes of budget left) and PROOF 57 drives the real handler over a chain spanning past the lease. Two mutations, each failing named examples. NOT CLAIMED: this is per-pass-on-cadence, not a background timer — a run whose passes are more than fifteen minutes apart still loses its lease, correctly, and the chain's own maximum gap is :444's 120 seconds. `entitlement_lease_expire` (the reclaim side) is S-22's and remains unbuilt.

open_decisions.title: Cancellation is PASS-BOUNDARY effective: it does not interrupt an already-authorized pass, so outbound requests may continue after it commits
open_decisions.authority: Owner decision at the S-07-009 acceptance boundary; recorded rather than taken inside the tranche
open_decisions.note: CURRENT BEHAVIOUR, WHICH IS COHERENT BUT INCOMPLETE. `CancelCrawl` prevents every LATER pass and the terminal checkpoint, because both re-read the Crawl and refuse a terminal one. It does NOT interrupt a pass already in flight: `Workflows::Wf005::CrawlDriver#advance` checks the run once at the top (`Admission#authorize_run`) and then performs its fetch, so after the cancellation commits one running pass may still make outbound requests and write `fetch_attempts` and `crawl_terminal_outcomes` rows. Those rows are INERT — the checkpoint never reads them, because it finds the Crawl terminal — but the outbound requests are OBSERVABLE CUSTOMER BEHAVIOUR: 'I cancelled and it fetched three more pages.' :442 requires in-flight cancellation at the WALL CLOCK and says nothing about `CancelCrawl`, so this is unratified rather than violated. THE DECISION IS BETWEEN TWO OPTIONS AND MUST BE EXPLICIT. (1) PASS-BOUNDARY CANCELLATION: ratify the current behaviour and disclose it. (2) IN-PASS COOPERATIVE CANCELLATION: the driver rechecks authoritative Crawl state at defined safe boundaries — before robots access, before a sitemap request, before each redirect hop, before the content request. THE OWNER'S STATED PREFERENCE IS (2), EVENTUALLY IMPLEMENTED WITH FU-28, because bounded outbound units provide natural cancellation boundaries without holding locks or polling repeatedly through one large pass. PER-REQUEST CANCELLATION MUST NOT BE IMPLEMENTED OPPORTUNISTICALLY: it affects locking, database traffic, outbound guarantees and the FU-28 checkpointed-execution design, all of which are decided together or not at all. UNTIL THAT WORK LANDS THE RECORD SAYS CANCELLATION IS PASS-BOUNDARY EFFECTIVE, and it is disclosed in `Workflows::Wf005::Handlers::CancelCrawl`'s own documentation rather than left to be discovered. RELATED: the identical question does not arise for the terminal checkpoint, which cannot race a pass into a false state because the frontier guard and the Crawl guard both refuse the writes that would matter.

reconciliation_note: S-07-012 ACCEPTED 2026-07-30 (ADR-096), and the honest summary of how is that the record was wrong twice before it was right. Two review rounds found and closed every blocking defect in the DRIVER; a third round, run against the accepted state as ADR-080 requires, found that the F-04 lease work committed alongside it was recorded as complete while one of three lease writers still disagreed. The lesson carried forward is structural, not procedural: a behavioural example that restates the implementation's own numbers proves nothing, and the checks that would have caught this are the ones that read the DOCUMENT and the CATALOGUE (spec/architecture/scheduled_action_lease_rule_spec.rb, PROOF 25) rather than the code's own arithmetic. Verified at implementation_commit f2b576e from a database built FROM EMPTY: rspec 1977/0; brakeman, packwerk, zeitwerk and bundler-audit clean; verify_runtime 15 checks with RLS intact; no structure drift.

excluded_contamination.owner_ruling: 2026-07-29, carried forward unchanged. Published history is NOT rewritten to make a tranche cosmetically clean. Unrelated files are EXCLUDED from the acceptance diff and the contamination is recorded here, attributed to the commit that introduced it.
excluded_contamination.reason: FOUR UNRELATED AUTHORIZED COMMITS FALL INSIDE THIS RANGE, and each is attributable to itself rather than to S-07-012. 4ad2520 is branding and operations collateral. cb42e39 is an authorized dependency-security repair patching Rails to 8.1.3.1 for CVE-2026-66066. 0c1aa43 and 63e3695 are the ADR-084 test-harness repair that bounded the shared raw PG connections (FU-15), and they touch spec/support and spec/architecture: a wholesale `spec/` claim would have absorbed that repair into this tranche's acceptance, which is exactly why the accepted paths are named FILE BY FILE rather than as `app/` and `spec/`.

acceptance_evidence.verified: The path-scoped diff plus the excluded set together account for every file changed in the range; nothing falls outside both. Asserted mechanically by spec/architecture/repository_truth_spec.rb, which now DERIVES the report it checks from acceptance_evidence.block instead of naming S-07-008 by hand. Until this transition that check validated a superseded tranche's record while the record actually being accepted was checked by nothing, which S-07-012's own report had declared as an open gap.
acceptance_evidence.note_on_range: THE RANGE IS BOUNDED AT BOTH ENDS, carrying forward the correction ADR-083's record already made. The endpoint is implementation_commit and it is deliberately NOT the acceptance commit: writing a SHA into this file changes that file's own commit SHA, and amending to close the loop orphans the recorded object, which the repository-truth check catches as unreachable. Later authorized commits touching other paths are attributable to THEMSELVES, not to this tranche, so the partition stays re-checkable at any head.
